items.title: fix(ai): preserve encrypted reasoning when resuming tool calls (#150633)
items.summary: fix(ai): preserve encrypted reasoning when resuming tool calls (#150633) Related: #150643 ## What Problem This Solves Managed Chat Completions can lose the encrypted state needed to continue after tool calls, or retain an old call's state when its streamed identity changes. ## User Impact Tool continuations retain only matching opaque state without exposing it as reply text, including when visible reasoning is off. ## Why This Change Was Made Both transport modes use the existing response-local tracker. An identity change retires the old association and only the signature that tracker still owns; direct first-ID behavior and independently written Google signatures remain intact. No configuration, schema, SDK, or replay-filter change. ## Evidence - On main `5764fa493344`, real `chat.send` and file reads reached a second HTTP request without the encrypted detail; the synthetic endpoint rejected it. On parent `6eb2f3c645eb`, both identity-change sequences carried stale state in the actual next request and persisted history. The correction passes those checks. - The current integration passes the unchanged ten-scenario Gateway/HTTP/read-tool regression, all four activation cases, the existing session-reclamation responsiveness test, and 290 focused provider/replay/redaction tests across nine files. - The first combined local run exceeded the continuation timeout and reclamation latency bound while static checking overlapped. The diagnostic and final serial runs passed under the original limits; no timeout or assertion was relaxed. The initial failures are retained in review evidence. - Scoped type-aware lint/type checking, registration lint, formatting, and the PR-owned structural checks pass. Required hosted CI remains the merge gate. ```sh node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server-isolated.config.ts src/gateway/server.encrypted-tool-continuation.test.ts ``` Coverage includes arrival order, signed and unsigned calls, ID replacement, delayed old details, reasoning visibility, malformed calls, missing termination, and real cancellation. The endpoint, credentials, and opaque state are synthetic; this is not a claim of live-provider prevalence or native-runtime coverage. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: fix(sqlite): name the failing read-only inspection operation (#149516)
items.summary: fix(sqlite): name the failing read-only inspection operation (#149516) Closes #149480 ## What Problem This Solves A readable SQLite database can appear unreadable when inspection actually fails to open its separate coordinator or private snapshot, because the diagnostic does not identify the failed operation. ## User Impact Inspection errors name the failed coordinator, source-database, or snapshot operation and retain the native SQLite codes. This improves diagnosis; it does not change permissions, retry policy, or admission. A failed agent remains unavailable without taking healthy agents or the Gateway down. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing operation owners attach bounded diagnostic context without replacing the original error. Both inspection transports use the same formatter, and the reusable schema reader preserves the diagnostic when restoring a typed state error. Native source and snapshot callers supply their actual operation. The change preserves local error identity, causes, native codes, exclusion and cleanup. It adds no schema, configuration, protocol, or persistence change. Diagnostic context contains fixed labels and bounded codes, not extra paths, SQL, environment values, or cause prose. The integration retains the current reusable-reader path introduced by #151366 rather than restoring its retired one-shot schema-header entrypoint. ## Evidence The original reproduction produced a generic `unable to open database file` even though the source database was readable. Fresh synthetic macOS Gateway proof at `cd89a83de5ba` exercised the supported `chat.metadata` request with only the agent's derived coordinator obstructed. It returned `UNAVAILABLE` with: ```text AgentDatabaseAdmissionError: failed while acquiring its state-handles coordinator: unable to open database file (code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR, errcode=14) ``` The native suffix appeared once. An independent `agents.list` request succeeded and reported the affected agent as degraded. Removing the obstruction and restarting restored the identical metadata request. Source bytes, session rows, schema metadata and integrity were unchanged after warmup; health remained HTTP 200 and normal shutdown exited 0. Native reader proof also exercised snapshot-open refusal, child settlement before rejection, healthy replacement requests, reacquired leases, and unchanged data. Frozen-error regressions protect original error identity and bounded metadata. The five focused SQLite files cover 107 passing cases on the integrated source, including the reusable schema reader, operation diagnostics, source leases, snapshot worker, and schema-header lifetime. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. The supported CLI rebuilt successfully, and all 13,099 generated records remained unchanged during the Gateway capture. Required hosted CI owns the complete selected matrix; historical failures are not relabeled by these focused local results. Scope limits: synthetic macOS state only; snapshot read denial requires non-root POSIX permissions. No provider request, Windows/Seatbelt claim, operator-service test, or general permission repair is claimed. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
